target_customer: Young urban adults paying per event to meet other groups of friends over drinks
problem: Meeting new people one-on-one through online dating is awkward; Grouper packaged a group outing of three friends meeting three others.
business_model: Consumer pay-per-event (members paid per Grouper evening; exact price not verified)

founders.name: Tom Brown
prior_employers: MoPub (early employee; acquired by Twitter, reported $350M)

technical_complexity.rationale: A web app for signup, matching of friend groups and venue booking; the hard part was operations, not technology.

defensibility.rationale: Event-matching service with local operations; no proprietary technology or network effects evidenced and the concept was easy to imitate.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent action found. Grouper partnered with Airbnb and Hipmunk (Oct 2012) and Uber (Jan 2013) for promotions.

market_need_then: Grouper reported tens of thousands of drinks shared within months of its summer 2011 NYC start and expanded to major US cities, suggesting early demand (company claim on YC page).
outcome_analysis: Grouper expanded to about 25 cities and had at least 30 staff, then in June 2014 shut its international operations and laid off staff, and Wikipedia dates its shutdown to October 2016. No reason was stated in the sources read and no funding totals were found, so the failure factors are inferred from the pattern of expansion then retrenchment and are low-confidence; the company did not publish a post-mortem that was found.
notes: Failure factors are inference, not stated by company or press. Search results mention a later relaunch of 'the new Grouper' as a mobile app (undated, Medium post) and an Entrepreneur list of apps that disappeared in 2016; neither was read. Funding amounts unknown; not zero. Competitors not recorded: no sources dated near 2012 retrieved.
